title: Splice a Chain Into a Gap
statement:
You get two singly linked lists, list1 and list2, and two positions a ≤ b (0-based) in list1.

Cut out the nodes of list1 at positions a through b, both included, and put the whole of list2 in their place. Return the head of the resulting list.

Positions are chosen so that at least one node stays on each side of the cut.

examples.why: Positions 2 and 3 hold 7 and 8. They are replaced by 1, 2.
When a = b exactly one node goes. The inserted chain can be longer than what it replaces.
Both ends are inclusive: 2, 3 and 4 all go. Stopping at position b − 1 would leave the 4 behind.

hints: You need two nodes of list1: the one just before the cut and the one just after it.
Walk to position a − 1 (call it before) and to position b + 1 (call it after). You also need the tail of list2.
Set before.next = list2, walk list2 to its last node, and set that node's next = after.

explain.intuition:
Splicing a chain is two re-links. The node just before the gap must point to the start of list2, and the end of list2 must point to the node just after the gap. Everything else stays put. It is the same as replacing a range of siblings in a DOM list with a fragment: you only touch the neighbours of the range.

Because a ≥ 1, the head never changes, so there is no special case for the start of the list.
steps: Walk from list1 to the node at position a − 1; call it before.
Keep walking to the node at position b + 1; call it after.
Walk list2 to its last node and set its next to after.
pitfalls: Off by one at the end of the cut: b is removed too, so the link goes to position b + 1.
Linking before to list2 before finding after, and then walking from before into list2 by mistake.
Forgetting to reach the tail of list2, which leaves the rest of list1 cut off.

solutions.title: Copy into an array and rebuild
solutions.idea: Read both lists into arrays, glue the slices together, and build a fresh list.

solutions.title: Two re-links
solutions.idea: Find the node before position a and the node after position b, then hook list2 in between.
solutions.py:
class Solution:
    def spliceInto(self, list1: Optional[ListNode], a: int, b: int, list2: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        before = list1
        for _ in range(a - 1):
            before = before.next
        after = before
        for _ in range(b - a + 2):  # from position a - 1 to position b + 1
            after = after.next
        before.next = list2
        tail = list2
        while tail.next:
            tail = tail.next
        tail.next = after
        return list1

followups: Allow a = 0 or b = list1.length − 1. Which special cases appear, and how does a dummy head remove them?
list2 is circular, and you are given a node in it to start from. How do you splice it in as a straight chain?
